patterns.title: Unit-digit cycles
patterns.spotTrigger: the unit digit of a big power
patterns.formula: Powers of 2, 3, 7, 8 repeat every 4 steps. Digits 0, 1, 5, 6 never change.
patterns.example: Unit digit of 7¹⁰³?
patterns.solution: 103 ÷ 4 leaves 3, and 7³ = 343, so the unit digit is 3.
patterns.shortcutTip: Use the remainder after ÷ 4. If it is 0, use the 4th power.

patterns.title: Remainder shortcut
patterns.formula: aⁿ ÷ (a − 1) leaves 1. Also a ≡ −1 (mod a + 1), so (−1)ⁿ decides the remainder.
patterns.example: Remainder when 5⁴⁵ is divided by 6?
patterns.solution: 5 ≡ −1 (mod 6) and 45 is odd, so (−1)⁴⁵ = −1, i.e. remainder 5.
patterns.shortcutTip: A negative remainder? Add the divisor.

patterns.title: Factors and HCF × LCM
patterns.spotTrigger: number of factors, or a missing number from HCF and LCM
patterns.formula: N = pᵃqᵇ has (a + 1)(b + 1) factors. For two numbers, HCF × LCM = their product.
patterns.example: HCF 12, LCM 180, one number 36. The other?
patterns.shortcutTip: 72 = 2³·3² has 4 × 3 = 12 factors.

patterns.title: Square and product tricks
patterns.spotTrigger: squares ending in 5, or products near a round number
patterns.formula: (n5)² = n(n + 1) followed by 25. a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).
patterns.example: Find 49 × 51 and 65².
patterns.shortcutTip: Look for ± the same distance from a round number.

patterns.title: Fraction–percent table
patterns.shortcutTip: Use the fraction for odd percentages, the % itself for round ones.

patterns.title: Net effect formula
patterns.spotTrigger: two successive changes, or price × consumption
patterns.formula: Net % = x + y + xy/100 (use a minus sign for a fall).
patterns.example: Price +25%, consumption −20%. Change in expenditure?
patterns.shortcutTip: The same formula handles successive discounts.

patterns.title: Mark-up and discount
patterns.spotTrigger: marked price, discount and profit together
patterns.example: Cost ₹800, mark-up 25%, discount 10%. Profit %?
patterns.shortcutTip: Equal SP with p% gain and p% loss gives a loss of p²/100 %.

patterns.title: Reverse percentage
patterns.formula: Number = N ÷ x × 100
patterns.example: 40% of a number is 120. Find it.

patterns.title: CI − SI shortcut
patterns.spotTrigger: the difference between CI and SI
patterns.shortcutTip: Money doubles under SI in 100/r years.

patterns.title: Effective rate
patterns.formula: Treat each year as a successive change: x + y + xy/100.
patterns.example: CI on ₹5,000 at 10% for 2 years?
patterns.shortcutTip: CI = amount − principal.

patterns.title: Unit method
patterns.spotTrigger: a ratio with a total or a difference
patterns.formula: One unit = total ÷ sum of the parts.
patterns.example: Ratio 7 : 9, sum 128. The larger number?
patterns.shortcutTip: If a difference is given, divide by the difference of the parts.

patterns.title: Alligation
patterns.spotTrigger: mixing two items at two prices or strengths
patterns.formula: Cheaper : Dearer = (Dearer − Mean) : (Mean − Cheaper)
patterns.example: Milk at ₹40/L and ₹60/L is mixed to give ₹46/L. Ratio?
patterns.shortcutTip: Dearer minus mean goes with the cheaper item.

patterns.title: Average change
patterns.spotTrigger: one value replaced, or a member added
patterns.formula: New average = old average + (new − old)/n
patterns.example: 8 numbers average 15. Replace 23 by 31. New average?
patterns.shortcutTip: Vessel: left = V(1 − x/V)ⁿ. 40 L, replace 10 L twice: 40 × (3/4)² = 22.5 L.

patterns.title: LCM units
patterns.spotTrigger: time and work, pipes and cisterns
patterns.formula: Take the LCM of the days as total work. Units per day = total ÷ days.
patterns.example: A takes 12 days, B takes 18. Together?
patterns.solution: Total 36. A = 3, B = 2 per day. 36 ÷ 5 = 7.2 days.
patterns.shortcutTip: An outlet pipe counts as negative units.

patterns.title: Efficiency ratio
patterns.formula: Efficiency ∝ 1/time. 25% better means efficiency 5 : 4, so time 4 : 5.
patterns.example: A is 25% more efficient than B. B takes 20 days. A?
patterns.shortcutTip: Wages are shared in the ratio of work done.

patterns.title: Trains and relative speed
patterns.spotTrigger: trains crossing a pole, a platform or each other
patterns.formula: Opposite: S₁ + S₂. Same direction: S₁ − S₂. Time = total length ÷ relative speed. km/h × 5/18 = m/s.
patterns.example: Trains of 100 m and 150 m at 40 and 60 km/h, opposite. Crossing time?
patterns.shortcutTip: Pole: only the train. Platform: add its length.

patterns.title: Average speed and boats
patterns.formula: Average = 2xy/(x + y). Still water = (D + U)/2. Current = (D − U)/2.
patterns.example: Downstream 18, upstream 10 km/h. Still water and current?
patterns.shortcutTip: 40 and 60 km/h over equal distances: 2·40·60/100 = 48.

patterns.title: x + 1/x family
patterns.formula: x² + 1/x² = k² − 2. x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k.
patterns.example: x + 1/x = 5. Find x² + 1/x².
patterns.shortcutTip: If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2.

patterns.title: Sum and product
patterns.formula: a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab. Roots of ax² + bx + c: sum −b/a, product c/a.
patterns.example: a + b = 11, ab = 24. Find a² + b².
patterns.shortcutTip: (a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab.

patterns.title: Cubes with zero sum
patterns.formula: a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc
patterns.example: a = 2, b = 3, c = −5. Find a³ + b³ + c³.
patterns.shortcutTip: Check the sum first; it unlocks the whole expression.

patterns.title: Factor theorem
patterns.formula: Put x = a: f(a) = 0.
patterns.example: x³ + ax² − 5x + 3 has factor (x − 1). Find a.
patterns.shortcutTip: The remainder on dividing by (x − a) is f(a).

patterns.title: Triangle centre angles
patterns.spotTrigger: angles at the incentre, circumcentre or orthocentre
patterns.formula: ∠BIC = 90° + A/2. ∠BOC = 2A (acute triangle). ∠BHC = 180° − A.
patterns.example: In △ABC, ∠A = 60°. Find ∠BIC.
patterns.shortcutTip: I: angle bisectors. O: perpendicular bisectors. H: altitudes.

patterns.title: Similar triangles
patterns.spotTrigger: a line parallel to a side, or ‘similar’ in the stem
patterns.formula: Sides k, perimeter k, height k, area k².
patterns.example: Similar triangles with sides 3 : 5. Ratio of areas?
patterns.shortcutTip: DE ∥ BC gives AD/DB = AE/EC.

patterns.title: Circle theorems
patterns.formula: Centre angle = 2 × circumference angle. Semicircle = 90°. Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles 180°. Tangent length = √(d² − r²).
patterns.example: A point is 13 cm from the centre; radius 5. Tangent length?
patterns.shortcutTip: Tangents from one external point are equal.

patterns.title: Common tangents and polygons
patterns.formula: Direct tangent √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²). Transverse √(d² − (r₁ + r₂)²). Regular polygon: exterior angle 360°/n.
patterns.example: Circles of radius 8 and 3, centres 13 apart. Direct tangent?
patterns.shortcutTip: Diagonals of an n-gon: n(n − 3)/2.

patterns.title: Solids at a glance
patterns.formula: Cone: l = √(r² + h²), CSA = πrl, V = ⅓πr²h. Sphere: 4πr², ⁴⁄₃πr³. Hemisphere TSA = 3πr².
patterns.example: Cone with r = 7 and h = 24. CSA?

patterns.title: Recasting and scaling
patterns.spotTrigger: melting, reshaping, percentage change in dimensions
patterns.formula: Volume stays the same. Scale by k: area k², volume k³.
patterns.example: A sphere of radius 3 is melted into spheres of radius 1. How many?
patterns.shortcutTip: Radius +10% means area +21%.

patterns.title: Cuboid and triangle area
patterns.spotTrigger: space diagonals, area from three sides
patterns.formula: Cuboid diagonal √(l² + b² + h²); cube diagonal a√3. Heron: √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)).
patterns.example: Triangle with sides 13, 14, 15. Area?
patterns.shortcutTip: Equilateral triangle: (√3/4)a².

patterns.title: Standard value trick
patterns.formula: sin = √0/2, √1/2, √2/2, √3/2, √4/2. cos is the reverse. tan = sin ÷ cos.
patterns.example: tan 45° + sin 30°?
patterns.shortcutTip: Write the sin row once; the rest follows.

patterns.title: Identities with a triangle
patterns.formula: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ
patterns.example: tan θ = 3/4. Find sec θ.
patterns.shortcutTip: Draw the right triangle: here 3-4-5.

patterns.title: Heights and distances
patterns.formula: tan = height ÷ distance. 30° gives 1/√3, 45° gives 1, 60° gives √3.
patterns.example: Shadow 10√3 m, sun at 30°. Height?
patterns.shortcutTip: Draw the triangle first and label the angle.

patterns.title: Complementary pairs
patterns.formula: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ. tan θ · tan(90° − θ) = 1.
patterns.example: tan 10° · tan 80°?
patterns.solution: tan 80° = cot 10°, so the product is 1.
patterns.shortcutTip: In a long product, pair θ with 90° − θ.

patterns.title: % change and pie angle
patterns.formula: % change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100. Pie angle = % × 3.6°.
patterns.example: Sales rise from 150 to 180. Growth? Angle of a 25% sector?
patterns.shortcutTip: Always divide by the old value.

patterns.title: Compare without dividing
patterns.spotTrigger: which fraction or ratio is larger
patterns.formula: Cross-multiply: a/b vs c/d means compare ad and bc.
patterns.example: Which is larger, 7/9 or 5/6?
patterns.shortcutTip: Round first; be exact only when options are close.

patterns.title: Mean, median, mode
patterns.formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean
patterns.example: Mean 20, median 18. Mode?
patterns.shortcutTip: Adding a constant keeps SD; multiplying by k multiplies SD by |k|.

patterns.title: Probability
patterns.formula: P = favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes.
patterns.example: Two dice: probability the sum is 7?
patterns.shortcutTip: Ace from a deck: 4/52 = 1/13. ‘At least one’ = 1 − P(none).
